name: Altstadt Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Rattenberg is Austria's smallest town and delights visitors as the world-famous Glass Town with medieval flair and a traffic-free pedestrian zone.
preis: Free entry to old town and castle ruins; Augustinian Museum approx. €6.00
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; glass-blowing workshops and museums generally open Mon–Sat 09:00–18:00
beschreibung:
Overview

With fewer than five hundred inhabitants and an area covering merely eleven hectares, the historic Old Town of Rattenberg in the Tyrolean lower Inn Valley is the smallest municipality in Austria. Snuggled between the precipitous castle hill and the gentle curve of the River Inn, this urban jewel chartered in the 14th century has preserved its captivating medieval townscape virtually untouched. Rattenberg is internationally famous today as Tyrol's historic „Glass Town“, where traditional glass-blowing, crystal cutting, and engraving have been practiced for generations, drawing visitors from across the globe.

Route & Requirements

A walking tour through the entirely pedestrianized streets leads past brightly painted burgher residences featuring classic Inn-Salzach facades, decorative oriels, and intricate wrought-iron guild signs. In numerous show workshops, guests can watch master glassblowers shaping glowing hot glass and creating delicate works of art. A gently ascending forest trail brings walkers up to the Rattenberg Castle Ruins on Schlossberg hill, where an open observation bastion presents glorious panoramic views over the rooftops of the old town and the green Inn Valley. The historic cobbled lanes are largely barrier-free and flat; comfortable footwear is recommended for the brief walk up to the ruins.

Visit & Arrival

The old town is accessible at all times and, thanks to its car-free policy, serves as an oasis of tranquility. Glass studios, showrooms, artisan shops, and the impressive Augustinian Museum are generally open from Monday through Saturday during the summer season. Public transportation: The ÖBB stop Brixlegg and the nearby Rattenberg-Kramsach station provide seamless connections via the S-Bahn Tirol; from the platform it is only a short walk through the medieval town gate. By car, take the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Kramsach); designated visitor car parks are conveniently located at the eastern and western town entrances.

Tips

Stop for coffee and fresh homemade apple strudel or Sachertorte at traditional Konditorei Hacker in the heart of town. During the winter season, the town hosts the atmospheric Rattenberg Advent: artificial lighting and amplified music are deliberately avoided, allowing hundreds of candles, torches, and open fire bowls to illuminate the historic facades in a magical glow. A visit to the Augustinian Museum's Gothic cloister perfectly rounds off the day.
